problem: The lead says that writing 1 to a pin lets 'a weak internal pull-up' raise it, stated for all four ports. P0 has no internal pull-up at all, so a student who reads only the lead will write 1 to P0 and still see a floating pin.
fix: Say it once for the ports that have one: 'write 1 to the pin, so the driver stops holding it low; on P1, P2 and P3 a weak internal pull-up then raises it, and on P0 an external resistor does that job.'

problem: 'so an external load that drags the pin slowly cannot be misread as the value the software intended' is garbled. The point of reading the latch is that the pin voltage may be degraded by the load, so the hardware ignores the pin and uses the value the software last wrote.
fix: 'so a pin whose voltage has been dragged down by an external load cannot corrupt the byte that is written back; the latch always holds the value the software intended.'

problem: The header says 'Instruction (port is destination)', but the first two rows (MOV A,P1, MOV C,P1.0, MOV 30H,P1, ANL A,P1, ADD A,P1) have the port as the source, not the destination, and read the pin. The header contradicts its own rows.
fix: Label the column 'Instruction' and split the table into two blocks: 'port is the source (reads the pin)' and 'port is the destination (reads the latch)'.

where: Section 2, rule sentence after the table, and Quiz Q5 answer
problem: The separating rule is given as 'the port is the destination of a logical or bit instruction', but the table itself lists INC P1, DEC P1 and DJNZ P1,rel as latch reads, and they are neither logical nor bit instructions. A student can conclude DJNZ P1,rel reads the pin.
fix: 'The rule: if the instruction reads the port, changes that value and writes it back (the read-modify-write group), it uses the latch. Instructions that only read the port use the pin.'

problem: 'an LED or gate on P0 with no resistor never goes high' clashes with the LED wiring taught in Section 1 (anode to +5 V through a resistor, cathode to the pin). That sink wiring works on P0 without any pull-up; only a pin that must source current or drive a logic input needs the resistor.
fix: 'Without external pull-up resistors the P0 pin cannot be pulled to logic 1, so it cannot drive a logic gate input or source current into an LED. The sink-style LED of Section 1 (cathode to the pin) still works on P0.'
